div.head: II Em Prolog
div.ab: Eadmund cyning cyð eallum folce, ge yldrum ge gingrum, ðe on his anwealde synd, ðæt ic smeade mid minra witena geðeahte, ge hadedra ge læwedra, ærest, hu ic mæhte Cristendomes mæst aræran.
Eadmund cyning cyð eallum folce, ge yldrum ge gingrum, ðe on his anwealde syn, þæt ic smeade mid minra witena geðeahte, ge godra hada ge læwedra, ærest, hu ic mæhte Cristendomes mest aræran.

Ego Eadmundus rex mando et precipio omni populo seniorum ac iuniorum, qui in regimine meo sunt, quod inuestigans inuestigaui cum sapientibus clericis et laicis in primis, quomodo possem Christianitatem magis erigere.
Eadmund cyning cyð eallum folce, ge yldrum ge gingrum, ðe on his anwealde syn, ðæt ic smeade mid minra witena geðeahte, ge god[cund]ra hada ge læwedra, ærest, hu ic mæhte Cristendomes mest aræran.

I, King Edmund, inform all people, both high and low, who are under my authority, that I have been considering, with the advice of my councillors both ecclesiastical and lay, first of all how I could best promote Christianity.

King Edmund informs all people, both high and low, who are in his dominion, that I have been inquiring with the advice of my councillors, both ecclesiastical and lay, first of all how I could most advance Christianity.

Prolog. König Eadmund kündet allem Volke, so oberen wie unteren, welche in seinem Gebiete sind, dass ich nachsann mit Beirath meiner Witan, so geistlicher wie Laien, erstens, wie ich das meiste Christenthum aufrichten könnte.

Prologue. King Edmund makes known to all the people, higher as well as lower, who are in his dominion, that I have considered with the counsel of my witan, clerical as well as lay, first of all how I could most advance Christianity.
div.note: Base text K = H (Textus Roffensis), after I Em on a new line with a red initial; N = B (CCCC 383). B's ‘godra’ should be corrected to ‘godcundra’ (Liebermann).
